topics.title: Property Management Tool
topics.summary: A simple 1-20 door tool where repairs feed UpKeep's home record.
topics.detail: The low end is crowded and cheap: Innago, Avail, TurboTenant and Baselane are free for landlords; RentRedi is $12/mo yearly; TurboTenant Pro $199/yr up to 10 units. Buildium starts at $62/mo, DoorLoop at $199/mo, AppFolio needs 50 units. Small landlords still glue Sheets, texts and memory together and handle repairs by text. v1 (effort M): rent tracker (record only), repair requests linked to the UpKeep home record, lease vault with renewal reminders, tenant messages. No payments or screening in v1. Owner: Prop, with UpKeep for the home record. Risks: fair housing wording, Michigan source-of-income rule, tenant data breach law, payments (use a licensed processor). Next: Prop and UpKeep agree the unit-to-home link, build a mock with fake data, Max tests on one unit for 30 days.

topics.title: UpKeep Tech Certifications
topics.summary: OSHA 10 yes, but EPA lead-safe (RRP) is the real must-have in Detroit.
topics.detail: OSHA 10 Construction is a voluntary $59, 10-hour online card: worth it, not legally required. Legally needed: EPA RRP renovator (8-hour class, $200 to $305, 5 yrs) plus a $300 EPA Lead-Safe firm cert, since 91% of Detroit homes are pre-1978; and employer ladder training (free ALI course). Michigan limits unlicensed techs to minor plumbing (clogs, faucets, valves), electrical wiring of $100 or less, and no HVAC repair. Strongly recommended: Red Cross First Aid/CPR (~$100), NATE Ready-to-Work ($60). Look-good extras: EPA 608 Type I ($24.95), HVAC Excellence exams ($15), Nest Pro (free), a $10K bond (~$125/yr), background checks.
